description: Site: rfc8398.rs:338-356. The function converts U-label (smtputf8) to A-label via idna::domain_to_ascii(u_domain), then compares case-insensitively against r_domain (the rfc822Name domain). Assumes rfc822 carries A-label form per RFC 8398 §3. Real-world counter-example: some buggy CAs emit rfc822Name with the IDN domain in U-label form (which is RFC-non-conforming — rfc822Name is IA5String, technically restricted to ASCII — but the field is sometimes loaded with UTF-8 anyway, especially in test vectors). For those certs, idna::domain_to_ascii(u_domain) produces 'xn--caf-dma.example' and r_domain is still 'café.example' (or 'xn--caf-dma.example' if the CA pre-converted). The eq_ignore_ascii_case comparison fails silently. This is technically the lint's job (rfc822Name SHOULD be A-label-encoded) but the lint's error message ('rfc822Name SAN entry has no matching SmtpUTF8Mailbox; RFC 8398 §3 requires byte-identical local-part and A-label/U-label-equivalent domain') doesn't pinpoint the encoding issue. Better: also try idna::domain_to_ascii(r_domain) and compare both directions; report 'rfc822 domain is not in A-label form' as a sub-diagnostic when the two ASCII conversions match each other. Filed P2 because real-world hit rate is low (most CAs do A-label) but the silent diagnostic is bad UX.
title: mailbox_equivalent does not idna-convert the rfc822 domain — silently rejects RFC-non-conforming-but-real rfc822 U-label SANs
